opennyai_summary.facts:
2) The petitioners are claiming compensation according to provisions of Section 13(5) of the Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition and Development) Act, 1957 (for short 'the Act, Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:12818 1957') read with Schedule-I of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'the Act, 2013').
The National Thermal Power Corporation Limited (NTPC) submitted a proposal before the Central Government for acquisition of lands and thereafter,
a notification under Section 4 of the Act, 1957 was published on 04.02.2009 in the official gazette.
The land owners and the NTPC reached a conclusion and based on their written agreement, the amount of compensation was paid to the land oustee in the year 2014-2015 itself.
4) In WPC No. 4209 of 2022, the compensation was paid to the father of the petitioner on 03.06.2014 to the tune of Rs.14,95,520/- and the same was accepted without any objection.
The owners of the property without raising any objection accepted the compensation so paid by the NTPC in the year 2014-15.
The original owners of the property are still alive and they did not avoid the compensation so awarded to them but after 7 years, their sons filed WP(S) No. 2387 of 2022 claiming therein employment according to the Rehabilitation Policy.
In that writ petition, there was no averment with regard to inadequate compensation and that petition was disposed of reserving liberty in favour of the petitioners to make representation before the appropriate authority.
The petitioners made representation before the officials of the NTPC and in turn, it was observed that the claims of the petitioners would be considered in accordance with the Rehabilitation Policy of the State.
Thereafter, the petitioners filed these petitions taking the plea that the amount of compensation was not paid in accordance with the Act, 1957.
opennyai_summary.10_April_2024__arguments:
The fathers/mother of the petitioners including the petitioners accepted the compensation in the year 2014-15; they claimed employment and in the year 2022, they filed these petitions claiming enhanced compensation according to the provisions of the Act, 2013 and the Act, 1957.
Admittedly, the fathers/mother of the petitioners entered into agreements with NTPC and they accepted the amount of compensation.
They neither challenged the decision arrived at by the NTPC nor questioned the adequacy of the compensation so paid.
opennyai_summary.decision:
11) With regard to rehabilitation/employment as claimed by petitioners, the NTPC is directed to consider the claim of the petitioners strictly in accordance with the Rehabilitation Policy of the State.
The petitioners are permitted to make representations before the Competent Authority of NTPC and in turn, the said authority shall decide the representations of the petitioners preferably within a period of six months from the date of receipt of representation strictly in accordance with law.
The land owners/their legal representatives would be entitled to get employment or any other benefit available under the Rehabilitation Policy.
12) With the aforesaid observation(s), these writ petitions are disposed of.
